raw_affiliation_strings: Simon N. Wood is Reader, Department of Statistics, University of Glasgow, Glasgow G12 8QQ, United Kingdom . About half of this work was undertaken as part of my paid employment, for which I gratefully acknowledge the Universities of St. Andrews and Glasgow as well as United Kingdom Natural Environment Research Council (NERC) grants NER/T/S/1999/00072 and NER/T/S/2002/00142. I am also grateful to Mark Bravington and Sharon Hedley for particularly useful discussions of parts of this work during a Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO) funded visit to CSIRO Tasmania, and to Stefan Lang for help with the mixed model approach to GAM's on a visit to the University of Munich. Thanks also to an associate editor for making a number of very helpful suggestions, including the mixed model comparisons; an almost anonymous referee for further helpful comments; Miguel Bernal and Yorgos Stratoudaki for discussion, patience, and the examples that broke the existing methods, as well as their institutions, Instituto de Investigação das Pescas e do Mar (IPI–MAR) and Instituto Español de Oceanografía (IEO), for permission to use the egg data. Finally, my thanks to Charles Paxton whose systematic approach was a great help in uncovering the convergence issues that this article tries to fix, and to numerous other people at St. Andrews for stimulating discussions on GAM's in general
